original_question: Given two monic polynomials of the same degree, form their topological mating by extending each map to the circle at infinity via theta maps to d theta, gluing the two circles by identifying theta for the first polynomial with -theta for the second, and then shrinking each external ray for the two polynomials to a point. For which pairs of polynomials does the resulting topological mating correspond to a rational map of degree d?
target_in_paper: §2, Quasiconformal Surgery, Question 1: "Which matings correspond to rational functions?"
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual problem: it uses two monic polynomials of the same degree, describes the mating construction via the circle at infinity with boundary dynamics θ↦dθ, uses the orientation-reversing identification θ∼−θ, collapses external rays, and asks when the resulting quotient is realized by a rational map of degree d.
missing_details: The ambient field should be stated explicitly: the paper is discussing monic complex polynomials.
The common degree should be named as an integer d≥2.
The paper's target conclusion is that the quotient branched map should be conjugate to a rational function of degree d; "correspond to" is slightly less precise.

For a stand-alone formulation, one should say that the question concerns pairs for which the topological mating construction just described is actually defined; the paper leaves the precise hypotheses needed for that construction implicit.
It helps to specify the object produced by the construction: a branched self-map of the sphere obtained from the two compactified disks after collapsing external rays.

The nearby text records a known obstruction in the quadratic case (Tan Lei's obstruction for complex-conjugate limbs of the Mandelbrot set); this is contextual information attached to the question, not part of the question itself.
No quasiconformal-surgery existence clause or continuity clause should be folded into the refined question, because those are separate Question 2 and Question 3 in the same section.
refined_question: Let P,Q∈C[z] be monic polynomials of the same degree d≥2, and suppose the following mating construction is defined: compactify each dynamical plane by a circle at infinity on which the map acts by θ↦dθ, identify the two boundary circles by θ∼−θ, and then collapse every external ray of P and Q to a point, obtaining a branched self-map of the topological sphere. For which pairs (P,Q) is this mating conjugate to a rational function of degree d on the Riemann sphere?
justification: The draft is targeting the first mating problem in §2, "Quasiconformal Surgery." Immediately before the question, the paper defines mating exactly in the way your draft describes: two monic same-degree polynomials, compactification by a circle at infinity, boundary map θ↦dθ, identification θ with −θ, and collapsing external rays; it then says the result should be conjugate to a rational map of degree d. Right after the rabbit–basilica example, the paper asks verbatim, "Which matings correspond to rational functions?" The next sentence adds the nearby paper-specific context that Tan Lei proved a quadratic obstruction: such matings can exist only when the two quadratic polynomials are not in complex-conjugate limbs of the Mandelbrot set. Because this paper is a problem list rather than a theorem/proposition paper, there is no explicit equivalent reformulation to substitute. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
